# Counting one's own draw misses joint excess

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`own-count-misses-joint-excess` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](own-count-misses-joint-excess.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Formations each taking within what is given can together exceed it; with natural-number amounts, joint excess cannot outlast what was held. Where renewers depend on what they renew, it ends the renewal and those depending at such a need, a taker among them where it so depends.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Formations take each within what is given across a step when no formation taking part takes from the condition more than the step gives it (Flow.WithinOwn), and jointly within what is given when their total take is at most what is given (Flow.WithinJoint). Each can take within what is given while together they take more. (`Becoming.Flow.WithinOwn`, `Becoming.Flow.WithinJoint`, `Becoming.Pair.flow`, `Becoming.Pair.own_not_joint`)
2. In a balanced flow, taking jointly within what is given keeps the level; a step of joint excess lowers it by at least one, so n consecutive steps of joint excess need a level of at least n at the start, and with two formations each taking a unit at every step and one unit given back no web balances the flow. (`Becoming.Flow.Balances`, `Becoming.Flow.joint_keeps`, `Becoming.Flow.excess_lowers`, `Becoming.Flow.excess_bounded`, `Becoming.Pair.no_web`)
3. Where every formation giving to the condition depends on it at a need of at least m, only active formations give (Acting) and activity needs support (Dependent), a level below m stays below m at every later step, and every formation depending on the condition at a need of at least m is inactive from then on. (`Becoming.Flow.Acting`, `Becoming.Flow.GiversSupported`, `Becoming.Flow.Acting.giversSupported`, `Becoming.Flow.stays_below`, `Becoming.Flow.ends_below`)
4. So n consecutive steps of joint excess from a level below n + m end the renewers and every formation depending on the condition at a need of at least m, a taker among them where it so depends; a taker not depending on it, or depending at a lower need, can continue. (`Becoming.Flow.joint_excess_ends`)
5. In Exceeding a renewer gives two units and two takers each take two, each within what the step gives; balance, Acting, Dependent and the gate hold, and from step two on none of the three is active (the ending is also stipulated in its activity, and the witness shows it consistent with these laws); with one taker the same renewer keeps the level and both are active at every step. (`Becoming.Exceeding.flow`, `Becoming.Exceeding.web`, `Becoming.Exceeding.balances`, `Becoming.Exceeding.acting`, `Becoming.Exceeding.dependent`, `Becoming.Exceeding.gated`, `Becoming.Exceeding.own_not_joint`, `Becoming.Exceeding.all_end`, `Becoming.Alone.flow`, `Becoming.Alone.web`, `Becoming.Alone.all_continue`)
6. The law of joint taking holds of every world in a local form, Flow.joint_keeps_at, with balance at the condition across the one step only; Flow.joint_keeps is its corollary. (`Becoming.Flow.BalancesOn`, `Becoming.Flow.Balances.on`, `Becoming.Flow.joint_keeps_at`)
7. So do the laws of excess and of the gate, needing only balance at the condition across the steps used (Flow.BalancesOn), gated givers supported there (Flow.GiversSupported), and the ending formation supported where active at that step; Flow.excess_lowers, excess_bounded, stays_below, ends_below and joint_excess_ends are their corollaries. (`Becoming.Flow.excess_lowers_at`, `Becoming.Flow.excess_bounded_at`, `Becoming.Flow.stays_below_at`, `Becoming.Flow.ends_below_at`, `Becoming.Flow.joint_excess_ends_at`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Balance: every change of a condition's level is what those taking part take and give.
- The gate: every formation giving to the condition depends on it at a need of at least m; only active formations give (Acting); activity needs support (Dependent). This is renewal depending on what it renews, not renewal in general.
- Excess is counted on totals at each step, not on shares; within what is given compares each taker with the whole of the step's giving.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- The gated conclusions hold only for renewal that depends on what it renews, not for renewal given from an outside source such as a sun.
- Stated for natural-number amounts; excess compares totals at each step and treats neither reserves nor delayed renewal.
- Exceeding and Alone are minimal witnesses; Exceeding's ending is stipulated in its activity and shown consistent with the laws. Witness: `Becoming.Exceeding.all_end`.
- The joint count binds only a want that outlasts what the condition holds, and a taker ends with it only where it depends at such a need.
- No instance theorem joins this result to the periphery's wear law; the link is interpretive.
- It does not say which taker ought to take less.
- Restates the tragedy of the commons and overshoot (Lloyd 1833, Hardin 1968, Meadows and others 1972); the laws are near-definitional arithmetic over natural numbers.
- **Counterexample:** Each within what is given is not enough to continue: in Exceeding each taker is within what is given and all three end after two steps (Exceeding.all_end); with one taker the same renewer and taker continue (Alone.all_continue). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Continuation.lean)
- **Counterexample:** A description in which joint excess goes on for ever is the flow of no balanced web: in Pair no web balances the flow (Pair.no_web). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Continuation.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision.

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Ren's proposal says that the self can become rigid and “has to count the dynamics that happens beyond what the "self" sees”. The periphery's wear law has the same phenomenon: where two parts are each within renewal and only jointly exceed it, the shared formation ceases with them (jointly_exceeding_parts_end_shared_formation in renewing-consuming-formation). This result states it on the spine, as a support-gated web and without the wear law: renewers depend on what they renew, joint excess brings the level below their need, renewal stops and those depending at such a need end, a taker among them where it so depends. The author's reading (an AI argument): the meta-attractor selects formations that take more; they form more at first and a count over a step prefers them; each counts its own draw, together they exceed renewal, the shared condition ends, and with it what depends on it at such a need, the winners among them where they so depend. A formation that wants its continuation beyond what the shared condition holds must count the joint draw on what it depends on; n steps of joint excess need only a level of n, so a want with a shorter horizon can be fully met amid joint excess (Mortal, see derived-extent-limits). This is what the want requires, not a verdict passed on it.
